decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.

Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [01, 02, 03, 05, 05, 06, 07. Received 06/08/2025].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.

Condition : 4 - Either side of the vehicle access hereby approved, visibility splay areas (the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, with a splay of at least 2.4 metres x 2.4 metres) shall be provided before the access and parking area is brought into use.  These areas shall be kept clear of any obstructions to visibility greater than 600 mm in height, including shrubs, planting, boundary walls, fences, gates, other means of enclosure or other structures or objects at all times.
Reason:  To ensure adequate visibility for drivers entering and leaving the site in the interests of pedestrian and vehicle safety.

Condition : 5 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, the existing vehicular access to the side/rear shall be permanently closed and the kerb and footpath reinstated so that it cannot be used as an access across the pavement.
Reason: In order to enhance the pedestrian environment and to confine vehicular access to the permitted points in order to ensure that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or highway safety along the adjacent highway.

Condition : 6 - The landscaping details shown on the submitted plans and documents shall be carried out as approved. 

The works shall comply with the requirements specified in BS 3936 (1992) 'Specification of Nursery Stock Part 1 Trees and Shrubs', and in BS 4428 (1989) 'Recommendations for General Landscape Operations'.

The details shall include (proposed finished levels or contours; means of enclosure; car parking layouts; other vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas; hard surfacing material; minor artefacts and structures (e.g. furniture, play equipment, refuse or other storage units, signs, lighting etc.); proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (eg drainage power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating lines, manholes, supports etc.); retained historic landscape features and proposals for restoration, where relevant). Soft landscape works shall include (planting plans; written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers/densities where appropriate; implementation programme).

All landscaping comprised in the approved details shall be carried out during the first planting and seeding seasons following completion of construction works or first occupation. Any trees or shrubs planted (including any such replacements) which die within five years from the date of planting shall be replaced in the next planting season with the same species, and of comparable maturity. The development shall be maintained in accordance with the approval.

Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area.

Condition : 7 - The hardstanding hereby permitted shall be made of porous materials, or include provision to direct surface water run-off to a permeable or porous area or surface within the application site, in accordance with the (then) Department for Communities and Local Government publication "Guidance on the permeable surfacing of front gardens" dated September 2008 before the development hereby permitted is first brought into use. The run-off shall not drain into any other foul or surface water drainage system. 
Reason: In order to reduce surface water run-off and the associated pressure on local drainage systems and so prevent flooding.
description: Formation of a vehicular access to the front and closure of existing vehicular access to the rear. Erection and alterations of boundary treatment. Part retrospective application for the hard standing to the front of the house and part reinstatement of soft landscaping to the front garden.
